eShop (the AdventureWorks online store): design-for-operations views

Drawn from the register example-eshop, as of 2026-08-28 (commit b4a4087), read 2026-10-08. These are design-time views for a production readiness review of one capability: what carries each step, where it could be seen and where it cannot, and whose cases a failure would hurt. They hold no live values.

The words

LevelWhat it meansExample, from this register
CapabilityWhat the business is able to do, named apart from how it is built. Covered by the flows that deliver it.Fulfil customer orders
Intended flowOne case's path from start to end, as designed.Fulfilling a customer's order
StageOne ordered stretch of a flow, with an entry and an exit.Accept the order
Process stepOne act inside a stage, with an outcome the business would recognise, that happened or did not.The order is released for stock checking when the grace period ends
ComponentA deployable part of the system that performs or supports a step. An AI agent is one.WebApp
External dependencySomething the system relies on and does not run.Webhook subscriber endpoint
CaseOne instance going through a flow, from its start to its end: what the business measures count.One order: a row of ordering.orders (Ordering.Infrastructure/EntityConfigurations/OrderEntityTypeConfiguration.cs:7; Ordering.Infrastructure/Migrations/OrderingContextModelSnapshot.cs:155-189)
WayOne route by which a step is carried out, where there is more than one. A step still happens while any one of its ways is whole.mobile, web
On recordA measure the register holds: proposed, or emitted by the code today. Never a reading.
Not assessedLooked for in the sources examined and not found, or not looked at. Never a finding that it is absent.
